gen-dafont-visitor-gf-geist: Nostalgic and a little glowing, Visitor sits on top. Geist, a plain sans, hums underneath with one quiet beat and no accents of weight, so the heading does all the talking.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-georama: Visitor's gaping e and short ascenders over big bowls give it a pixel-era wink. And Georama, in sans-serif dress, opens its c wide and keeps its capitals low, so paragraphs glide along without fuss.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-gidole: Gidole takes the body, its terminals held apart like scissor blades. Above it Visitor pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, and the neon-tube consistency below lets that retro heading stand out without a fight.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-golos-text: Retro pixels meet a modern face here, with Visitor's big bowls up top. Golos Text, a sans-serif with a tall x-height and widely parted s, keeps long reading easy.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hedvig-letters-san: Wire-like, digital, a bit nostalgic. Hedvig Letters Sans underneath leaves a clear gap at the end of each c and lifts its small letters nearly to capital height, so Visitor's tubular heading gets a body that reads easily for pages.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-heebo: Heebo is the workhorse here, a plain sans with a tall central band of text and curves that stop short. Heebo can sit a touch larger than you'd guess beneath Visitor, whose fixed-pressure stylus strokes already feel quite small.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-guntur: Visitor opens with gaping e shapes and short ascenders above big bowls, a clearly digital look. And Hind Guntur, a plain sans with no thick-thin shift, can go a little larger than usual because its tall lowercase stays compact.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-madurai: Hind Madurai fills the line with lowercase that behaves like capitals, and its s curves open wide at both ends. Under Visitor's nostalgic pixel heading, that sturdy sans makes a firm floor.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-mysuru: Gaping mouths on every e give Visitor an unmistakable retro-digital grin, with ascenders kept short over big bowls. Hind Mysuru, a sans with no calligraphic thinning, answers that quirk with a straight face.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-hind-siliguri: Nostalgic and digital, Visitor pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle at the top. But Hind Siliguri, a sans-serif of constant line weight and cracked-bangle rounds, hums flatly below, leaving the heading its spotlight.
